title: Initial snapshot
statement: Let $M$ be a finite binary Turing machine and let $x$ be a finite binary word. At time zero its snapshot consists of the initial state, the input symbol at position $1$ (the first bit of $x$, or blank if $x$ is empty), and a blank symbol under each work-tape head.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite binary Turing machine
replaced:
Let $M$ be a binary multi-tape Turing machine with initial state $q_0$ and $k$ work tapes,
and let $x \in \{0,1\}^*$. Before any step is taken, $M$ on input $x$ is in state $q_0$, the
symbol under its input head is the first bit $x_1$ of $x$ (or the blank $\sqcup$ if $x$ is
empty), and every one of its $k$ work heads reads the blank $\sqcup$.
